findings.evidence: `HasCartanType P b t := ∃ e : b.support ≃ Fin t.rank, …` (TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/DynkinType.lean:400) only gives an existential relabelling, so `hasCartanType_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum` does not recover the pinned Cartan integers. Mathlib's `RootPairing` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Defs.lean) defines `pairing i j` through `toLinearMap`, and `D.lean` has `public section` but no `@[expose]`, so the body giving `toLinearMap := dotProductBilin ℤ ℤ` (line 340) is not exported.
findings.fix: Make the pairing API public: add `theorem toLinearMap_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum : (typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum n hn).toLinearMap x y = x ⬝ᵥ y := rfl` (or make `pairing_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum` public), make `pairing_typeDSimpleIndex` public, and add the `@[simp]` fundamental-weight lemma `(typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum n hn).toLinearMap (Pi.single i 1) ((typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum n hn).coroot (typeDSimpleIndex n hn j)) = if i = j then 1 else 0`.
findings.issue: `pairing_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum` and `pairing_typeDSimpleIndex` (line 542) are `private`, and the datum's body is not `@[expose]`d, so `(typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum n hn).toLinearMap` is opaque downstream. No consumer can compute `⟨χ, coroot k⟩` for any character `χ`; in particular the fundamental-weight pinning `⟨ω_i, α_j^∨⟩ = δ_ij` that the module docstring (line 19) and the roadmap target both assert is unstatable, and even `pairing (typeDSimpleIndex i) (typeDSimpleIndex j) = CartanMatrix.D n i j` is unavailable.

findings.evidence: `typeDRootEquiv` (ClassicalTypeD.lean:317), `typeDSimpleRoot` (:423) and `typeDSimpleRootCoordinates` (:479) are all public defs; D.lean:359-362 states the coroot equation purely in those terms yet marks it `private`.
findings.fix: Make `coroot_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum` public as stated (it is `rfl`), and add the public root counterpart in classical terms: `(typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum n hn).root k = fun j => (typeDRootEquiv n hn k).1 ⬝ᵥ typeDSimpleRoot n hn j` (`typeDWeight` is private, so unfold it in the statement).
findings.issue: `root_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum` and `coroot_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum` (line 359) are `private`, so only the first `n` indices are characterized publicly and the datum is a black box on the remaining `2*n*(n-1) - n` roots. Their right-hand sides use only public declarations (`typeDRootEquiv`, `typeDSimpleRootCoordinates`, `typeDSimpleRoot`), so keeping the public `typeDRootEquiv` enumeration and then sealing off its link to the datum defeats the point of exposing it.

findings.evidence: `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/NumberOfRoots.lean:59`: `@[simp] lemma numRoots_D (n : ℕ) : (D n).numRoots = 2 * n * (n - 1) := rfl`. `grep -n "numRoots" D.lean` returns only lines 8, 55 (comment) and 353.
findings.fix: Delete the `example` and the now-unneeded `public import TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.RootSystem.NumberOfRoots`; the docstring sentence at line 53-55 already records the agreement, and `numRoots_D` is `rfl` so `Fin (D n).numRoots` is defeq to the index type anyway.
findings.issue: `example (n : ℕ) : (DynkinType.D n).numRoots = 2 * n * (n - 1) := numRoots_D n` is a verbatim restatement of the existing public `@[simp] lemma numRoots_D` and is the module's only use of `numRoots`; it is the sole reason for `public import TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.RootSystem.NumberOfRoots` (line 8), which re-exports that module to every consumer of `D.lean`.

summary: The exposed surface is minimal and free of compatibility artifacts, and the new ClassicalTypeD branch equations correctly avoid exposing typeDSimpleRoot's body. But the datum's perfect pairing and its general-index root/coroot equations are private, so downstream nothing can evaluate the pairing at all — the fundamental-weight pinning the docstring and roadmap assert is unprovable off the datum's own module.
